Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১) Amin took a loan of Tk.1400 with simple interest for as many years as the rate of interest. If he paid Tk.686 as interest at the end of the loan period, what was the rate of interest?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Given that T = R
S.I = (P × R × T)/100
⇒ 686 = (1400 × R × R)/100
⇒ 686 = 14R2
⇒ R2 = 49
⇒ R = 7.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২) A sum of money at simple interest amounts to Tk.815 in 3years and to Tk.854 in 4 years. What is the sum?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
S.I. for 1 year = 854 - 815
= 39
S.I. for 3 years = 39 × 3
= 117
∴ Required Sum = 815 - 117
= Tk. 698.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৩) A person borrows Tk.5000 for 2years at 4% per annum simple interest. He immediately lends it to another person at 6(1/4)%per annum for 2 years. Find his gain in the transaction per year.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
The difference in interest rate = 6(1/4)% - 4%
= (25/4)% - 4%
= (9/4)%
Gain per year
= simple interest on Tk. 5000 at = (9/4)% for 1 year.
= {5000 × (9/4) × 1}/100
= 225/2
= Tk. 112.5

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৪) A man took out a loan from a bank at the rate of 8%per annum simple interest. After 4 years he had to pay Tk. 6200 interest only for the period. What was the principal amount borrowed by him?
৫) A lends Tk. 1500 to B and a certain sum to C at the same time at 8% per annum. If A receives Tk. 1400 as simple interest from B and C after 4 years, then the sum lent to C is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum lent to C be x
Simple interest on Tk. 1500 at 8% for 4 years + simple interest on x at 8%for 4 years.
= Tk. 1400
(1500 × 8 × 4)/100 + (x × 8 × 4)/100 = 1400
⇒ {8 × 4(1500 + x)}/100 = 1400
⇒ 1500 + x = 4375
⇒ x = 4375 - 1500
⇒ x = 2875.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৬) A sum of Tk. 10 is given as a loan, to be returned in six monthly installments of Tk. 3.What is the simple interest rate?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the rate of interest be R%
Amount due in 6 months
= 10 + simple interest on Tk. 10 for six months.
= {10 + 10 × R × (1/2)}/100
= 10 + (R/20)
With the formula mentioned,
3 = 100(10 + 9R/20)/{(100 × 6) + R × 6(6 - 1)}/(2 × 12)
⇒ 3 = (1000 + 5R)/{600 + (5R/4)}
⇒ 1800 + 15R/4 = 1000 + 5R
⇒ 5R/4 = 800
⇒ R = 640.
Hence interest rate is 640%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৭) If the simple interest on a certain sum of money after 3(1/8) years is (1/4) of the principal, what is the rate of interest per annum?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum be x
Then,
Simple interest = x/4
T = 3(1/8)
= 25/8 years
R = {100 × (x/4)}/{x × (25/8)}
= 8
Hence Required interest rate = 8%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৮) If a sum of Tk. 9 is lent to be paid back in 10 equal monthly installments of Tk. 1 each, the rate of interest is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the rate of interest be R%
Amount due in 10 months
= 9 + simple interest on Tk. 9 for ten months
= 9 + {9 × R × (10/12)}/100
= 9 + (3R/40)
With the formula mentioned,
1 = 100{9 + 3R/40)}/[(100 × 10) + {R × 10(10 - 1)/(2 × 21)}]
900 + (15R/2) = 1000 + (15R/4)
15R/4 = 100
R = 26.67.
Hence the interest rate is 26.67%.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৯) In how many years, Tk. 150 will produce the same simple interest at 6% as Tk. 800produce in 2years at 4(1/2)%?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Assume,
Simple interest on Tk. 150 at 6% for n years
= simple interest on Tk. 800 of
(150 × 6 × n)/100 = {800 × (9/2) × 2}/100
150 × 6 × n = {800 × (9/2) × 2}
n = 8.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১০) A sum of money doubles in 12 years. In how many years, will it treble (assume simple interest)?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum be x Assume that it will treble in n years.
Note that when the money doubles, simple interest is (2x - x), and when the money trebles, simple interest is (3x - x)
simple interest ∝ T (because here P and R are constants)
Therefore,
(2x - x) : (3x - x) = 12 : n
⇒ x : 2x = 12 : n
⇒ n = 24.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১১) A man buys Tk. 20 shares paying 9% dividend. The man wants to have an interest of 12% on his money. What is the market value of each share?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Face value of each share = Tk. 20
Dividend per share = 9% of 20 = (9 × 20)/100
= 9/5.
He needs to have an interest of 12% on his money
Money Paid for a share = (9/5) × (12/100)
Money Paid for a share = (9/5) × (100/12)
= 15.
ie, Market Value of the share = Tk. 15.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১২) A man invested Tk. 1552 in a stock at 97 to obtain an income of Tk. 128. What is the dividend from the stock?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
By investing Tk. 1552, income = Tk. 128
By investing Tk. 97, income = (128 × 97)/1552
= 8
Hence, the dividend is 8%.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৩) 12500 shares, of par value TK. 20 each, are purchased from Rumon by Mahin at a price of Tk. 25 each. Find the amount required to purchase the shares.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Face value of each share = Tk. 20
The market value of each share = Tk. 25
Number of shares = 12500
Amount required to purchase the shares = 12500 × 25 = 312500.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৪) A man invested Tk. 26000 in 5% stock at 104. He sold the stock when the price rose to Tk. 120 and invested the sale proceeds in 6% stock. By doing this his income increased by Tk. 2500. At what price did he purchase the second stock?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Assuming that face value of the first stock = Tk. 100 as it is not given in the question.
Since it is a 5% stock, we can take the dividend per stock = Tk. 5
Market Value of the first stock = Tk. 104
Investment on the first stock = Tk. 26000
Number of stocks purchases = 26000/104 = 250
His total income from all these stocks = Tk. 250 × 5 = Tk. 1250
He sells each of these stocks at Tk. 120
ie, amount he earns = Tk. 120 × 250 = Tk. 30000
He invests this Tk. 30000 in 6% stock (here also face value is not given and hence take it as Tk. 100)
His new income = Tk. (1250 + 2500) = Tk. 3750
ie, By Tk. 30000 of investment, he earns an income of Tk. 3750
To get an income of Tk. 6, the investment needed = (30000 × 6)/3750
= Tk. 48.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৫) Jobayed buys 100 shares of par value Tk. 5 each, of a company, which pays an annual dividend of 12% at such a price that he gets 10% on his investment. Find the market value of a share.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Face value of each share = Tk. 5
Total dividend received by Jobayed = {100 × 5 × (12/100)}
= Tk. 60
Let market value of 100 shares = Tk. x
x × (10/100) = 60
x = 600
ie, Market value of 100 shares = Tk. 600
Hence, Market value of each share = Tk. 6

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৬) To produce an annual income of Tk. 800 from a 8% stock at 90, the amount of stock needed is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Since face value is not given, take it as Tk. 100.
As it is an 8% stock, income (dividend) per stock = Tk. 8
ie, For an income of Tk. 8, amount of stock needed = Tk. 100
For an income of Tk. 800, the amount of stock needed = (100 × 800)/8
= 10000

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৭) A man sells 4000 common shares of a Company x (each of par value Tk. 10), which pays a dividend of 40% at Tk. 30 per share. He invests the sale proceeds in ordinary shares of Company Y (each of par value Tk. 25) that pays a dividend of 15%. If the market value of Company Y is Tk. 15, find the number of shares of Company Y purchased by the man -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Just too much information is given in the question to confuse. This is a straight and simple question
Market Value of Company X (his selling price) = Tk. 30
Total shares sold = 4000
The amount he gets = Tk. (4000 × 30)
He invests this amount in ordinary shares of Company Y
Market Value of Company Y(His purchasing price) = 15
Number of shares of company Y which he purchases = (4000 × 30)/15
= Tk. 8000.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৮) A company issued 20000 shares of par value Tk. 10 each. If the total dividend declared by the company is Tk. 24000, find the rate of dividend paid by the company.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Number of shares = 20000
Face value of each share = Tk. 10
dividend per share = (10 × R/100) where R is the Rate of interest.
Total dividend = 20000 ×10 ×R/100
20000 ×10 ×R/100 = 24000
R = 24000/2000
= 12
Hence the dividend is 12%.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ১৯) Abir invested Tk 333000 in 5(1/2) % stocks at 110 .If brokerage is Tk. 1, what is his annual income from his investment.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Investment = Tk. 333000
Since face value is not given, we can take it as Tk.100
and dividend per share = Tk. 11/2
Market Value = 110 + 1 = 111
Number of shares purchased = 333000/111 = 3000
Total income = 3000 × (11/2)
= Tk. 16500.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২০) In order to obtain an income of Tk. 650 from 10% stock at Tk. 96, one must make an investment of -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Market Value = Tk. 96.
Required Income = Tk. 650.
Here face value is not given. Take face value as Tk. 100 if it is not given in the question
To obtain Tk. 10 (ie,10% of the face value 100), investment = Tk. 96
To obtain Tk. 650, investment = {(96/10) × 650}
= Tk. 6240.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২১) There is an 80% increase in an amount in 8 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest of Tk. 14,000 after 3 years at the same rate?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
80% increase in 8 years at simple interest. That is 10% each year.
Therefore,
Rate of interest is 10%
10% (14000) = 1400
10% (1400) = 140
10% (140) = 14
Required compound interest = 3(1400 + 140) + 14
= Tk. 4634.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২২) The difference between simple and compound interest(compounded annually) on a certain sum of money for 2 years at 4% per annum is Tk. 1.What is the sum?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
P(4/100)2 =1
⇒ P(1/25)2 = 1
⇒ P/252 = 1
⇒ P = 625
Hence The sum is Tk. 625.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৩) The effective annual rate of interest corresponding to a nominal rate of 6% per annum payable half-yearly is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Compound interest for 1 year.
2{3%(P)} + 3%{3%(P)}
= 6%(P) + 0.09%(P)
= 6.09%(P)
That is an effective interest rate for 1 year = 6.09%.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৪) If the difference between the simple interest and compound interests on some principal amount at 20% for 3 years is Tk. 48, then the principal amount is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum be Tk. x
Amount after 3 years on Tk. x at 20% per annum when interest is compounded annually
P(1 + R/100)T
= x{1 + (20/100)}3
= x(120/100)3
= x(6/5)3
Compound interest = {x(6/5)3 - x}
= x{(6/5)3 - 1}
= x{(216/125) - 1}
= 91x/125
Simple interest PRT/100 = (x × 20 × 3)/100
= 3x/5
Given that difference between compound interest and simple interest is Tk. 48
(91x/125) - (3x/5) = 48
⇒ (91x - 75x)/125 = 48
⇒ 16x/125 = 48
⇒ x = (48 × 125)/16
= 3 × 125
= Tk. 375.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৫) The population of a town is 40,000. It decreases by 20 per thousand per year. Find out the population after 2 years.
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
R = {(20 × 100)/1000)}
= 2% [percentage is calculated for twenty per thousand]
Population after 2 years
= P(1 - R/100)T
= 40000{1 - (2/100)}2
= 40000{1 - (1/50}2
= 40000(49/50)2
= (40000 × 49 × 49)/(50 × 50)
= 16 × 49 × 49
= 38416.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৬) On a sum of money, the simple interest for 2 years is Tk. 320, while the compound interest is Tk. 340, the rate of interest being the same in both the cases. The rate of interest is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Simple interest for 2 years is Tk. 320
⇒ Simple interest for first year = 320/2 = 160
⇒ Similarly, simple interest for the second year is also 160
Compound Interest for first year = 160
Compound Interest for second year = 340-160 = 180
we can see that compound Interest for the second year is more than
simple interest for the second year by 180-160 = 20
i.e., Tk. 20 is the simple interest on Tk. 160 for 1 year
R = 100 × S.I./PT
= (100 × 20)/(160 × 1)
= 12.5%

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৭) A bank offers 10% interest rate compounded annually. A person deposits Tk. 20,000 every year in his account. If he does not withdraw any amount, then how much balance will his account show after four years?
২৮) If a sum on compound interest becomes three times in 4 years, then with the same interest rate, the sum will become 81 times in -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum be P
The sum P becomes 3P in 4 years on compound interest
3P = P{(1 + R/100)}4
3 = {1 + R/100)}4
Let the sum P becomes 81P in n years
81P = P{1 + (R/100)}n
81 = {1 + (R/100)}n
34 = {1 + (R/100)}n
[{1 + (R/100)}4]4 = {1 + (R/100)}n
{1 + (R/100)}16 = {1 + (R/100)}n
n = 16.

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ২৯) The market value of a 10.5% stock, in which an income of Tk. 756 is derived by investing Tk. 9000, brokerage being (1/4 )%, is -
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Assume that face value = Tk. 100
Dividend per share = Tk. 10.5 (as it is 10.5% stock)
By investing Tk. 9000, earnings = Tk.756
To get an earning of Tk. 10.5, the investment required = (9000 × 10.5)/756
= Tk. 125
ie,market value of Tk. 100 stock = Tk.(125- 1/4) = Tk. 124.75

Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.question: ৩০) If a sum of money trebles itself in 40 years, what is the rate of interest?
Simple & Compound Interest, Stocks & Sha.exp:
Let the sum of money be x.
x becomes 3x in 40 years.
Simple interest = 3x -x
= 2x
R = (100 × 2x)/(x × 40)
= 5%
